notes.title: Townscaper's developer on how its 'radically casual' design is inspiring a new wave of low-stress builders to adapt the blueprint
notes.notes: Townscaper is one of those small snatches of joy I heavily associate with the Covid-19 lockdowns of 2020. The stress-free city builder was a tiny game that became a huge sensation that summer. Like other collective obsessions of that year, it inspired a trend that's only now truly coming to fruition. Although Townscaper's developer Oskar Stålberg tells me he doesn't spend time tracking gaming trends these days, he's aware of the wave of Townscaper-like projects in the works and often reshares their dev updates. He also tells me he thinks the new games in this style are getting more complex... Read more.

Dear Townscaper community,

We recently deployed an update which contained a number of optimization improvements that were developed while bringing Townscaper to additional platforms. Unfortunately, we've discovered some new issues caused by these changes and have temporarily reverted to an older version of the game.

notes.title: Townscaper is the latest surprise addition to Xbox Game Pass
notes.notes:
Townscaper, a chill and very aesthetically-pleasing city-builder from Oskar Stalberg (whom you may know as the developer behind Bad North) is now available to play on Xbox Game Pass.

Townscaper has long been something of a social media darling; if you mooch about games Twitter like me, you'll have seen it crop up often as other indie devs share little snippets of the towns and villages they've made. Buildings appear with a very satisfying 'pop' and the whole thing is more like a toybox experience than a traditional game. I urge you to give it a go if you've got the time, it's honestly a delight.

"Build quaint island towns with curvy streets, small hamlets, soaring cathedrals, canal networks, or sky cities on stilts. Build the town your dreams, block by block," reads a little blurb for the game. "No goal. No real gameplay. Just plenty of building and plenty of beauty. That's it."

Read more

notes.title: Nominate Townscaper for the Sit Back and Relax Award!
notes.notes:
Some games, like Townscaper, can be simultaneously gentle and impactful. There are no high stakes, and there is nothing that needs to be done.

Townscaper doesn't seek to change the world. Instead, it seeks to change a town, a town that can belong entirely to you.

With Townscaper, the hours melt away, no matter when or where. After a long day, hours spent at the PC or on the couch can become hours spent unwinding, creating something uniquely beautiful.

[i]And did we mention, there are tiny, tiny birds?
[/i]
With the 2021 Steam Awards fast approaching, we really hope you'd consider nominating us for the Sit Back and Relax award. If you, like us, have found yourself lost, and relaxed, building your own town, we hope you can find the time to check out the Steam Awards and vote for us.

It's time once more for us to shine a light on some of the inventive towns and ingenious builds we’ve recently seen from Townscaper's creative community. 

Each of these builds showcase an interesting way that Townscaper can be played to create something special and unique, so be sure to share your love in the comments and even use these builds to inspire your own! 


[b][u]TWITTER [/u][/b]

[b]1. [/b]Towns on towns on towns by @rinen33 
An image shared on Twitter by rinen333 shows three towns stacked upon one another. These towns are enclosed, symmetrical, and unique to each platform. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37915459/04c695e1af74220d1981d29a244ca76deec8a4a4.png[/img]

notes.title: Townscaper review - a city-builder without rules
notes.notes:
What's that? Look closer. It's water: a little eruption of it, a hopping splash of droplets. With each building you place in Townscaper, each new disturbance on its flat ocean, you get a splash of water to go along with the brisk, genial popping sound as you press the button. Pop! A ripple on the surface. And onto the next one.

Townscaper is a simple thing, as simple and clear as the face of a wristwatch. But like the face of a wristwatch, it pulls you in, its own little universe for you to peer down at and ponder for who knows how long. This is a game-like toy, an art tool in which you create - and erase, if you wish - little towns, starting with a still stretch of water and ending with busy centres, suburbs, cathedrals, tower blocks, hamlets, burgs, you name it. One button to place a building, one to remove it. Zoom in, change the colours of the next blocks you put down, drop the whole thing out to white box to make it look truly sculptural, change the position of the sun, take a screenshot, tinker away some more.

It's brilliant.

Read more

notes.title: Townscaper review
notes.notes: Of all the places I lived growing up, I've a particular fondness for the seaside town of North Berwick, waking up a stone's throw from the rolling waves and screaming gulls, salty air wafting through winding streets. Going back these days breaks the illusion a little, mind—the town's been further gentrified into a resort, and you can barely move for tourists at the height of summer. Fortunately, Swedish developer Oskar Stålberg's Townscaper recaptures the magic of exploring an endless series of quaint ports and seaside villages, one tile at a time... Read more.

notes.title: Surprise — Townscaper is officially launched!
notes.notes:
Dear Townscapers,
 
The time has come to venture out of Early Access and call this latest version 1.0. 

[previewyoutube=4SjAuF81c0c;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

[b]Some changes include:[/b]
 
[list]
[*] A larger grid (unless you build very very tall)
[*] A mesh exporter (because I wanna see people make 3D prints)
[*] Performance improvements (that should be quite noticeable in larger towns)
[*] The ability to remap (and actually see) the keyboard controls.
[*] Gamepad support.
[/list]
 
Many of you have dreamed of larger changes and bigger features. While I am afraid we don't have further development plans at this point, I am glad and humbled the game has sparked your imagination. 
 
I have spent the last year off and on my ridiculously long Swedish parental leave. What little work time I’ve had, I’ve spent fixing bugs, working with Raw Fury on the additional platform releases, and admiring your beautiful Townscaper creations.
 
As always, let us know if you find any bugs.
 
Many thanks for all the love,
Oskar Stålberg

I finally made the obviously good choice to let him. He did not disappoint on Bad North, and he did not disappoint here. All the plops and blips are now 80% more professional and 120% more pleasant.

I also fixed some visual bugs introduced with an optimization in the last update, where some specific block configurations would break and create big holes in the mesh. There might still be more of these lurking, so please do report if you come across them. 

Apparently, under some rare conditions, the game can produce broken save files. That's sad, and I don't know how to fix it. But those save files also broke the whole game, which I do know how to fix. So that's fixed now. This should fix some terrible loading bugs or crashes some of you have been having.

As this year begins, I am transitioning from 50% parental leave to 100% parental leave. I look forward to spending loads of time with my daughter, but obviously it will mean even less time to work on Townscaper.

For me, 2020 was great. Sadly, I have been informed that for some of you 2020 was not so great. I would therefore like to wish you all a very good 2021.

Oskar Stålberg[/i]

On the plus side, that rewrite provided some optimization to the core algorithm, and also opened up for some other minor architectural elements that were previously not possible.

I also fixed some seams and discontinuities in the grid (caused by floating point errors). These errors would appear when you build far out from the center of the world. With the new grid I'm kinda encouraging you to do that, so I felt it was thus becoming to adress that bug.

notes.title: Circular towns hovering in the sunset
notes.notes:
A nice chunky update to all my dear townscapers

[h3]Square grid! Round grid! Loopy grid![/h3]
I've scattered some special hand made sections around the grid. These sport features like perfect loops, various types of symmetry, large square sections, etc. When you start a new town you can go search for one of these special places and start building there.

[h3]Flying towns![/h3]
Apparently, it was always possible to create flying structures by finding rare perfect loops in the grid. With the new special grid sections there are many more such perfect loops to be found. And the flying structures now get little propellers to help them stay up without any legs

[h3]Sunlight, shadows and sunsets![/h3]
I added some subtle sunlight that cast even subtler shadows. You can control where the sun comes from and how far up the horizon it is.

[h3]High res screenshots![/h3]
There's now a button to take high res screenshots! Take many screenshots and fill all social media channels with them! Print them out and post them to your relatives!

[h3]Fast undo/redo![/h3]
Pretty minor, but if you hold down undo or redo, it will now undo or redo really fast, which looks kinda cool.

[h3]Breaking saves![/h3]
Unfortunately, my changes to the grid will break some of your saves. I've made sure not to change the grid close to the starting area, so unless you traveled very far out to start building, your town should be safe. My apologies if I broke your town, but this is Early Access.

[i](If you still wanna save your broken town, I've created a legacy branch called 0.14, which contains the game as it was before this update, including your old saves, frozen in time)[/i]


[i]Best wishes
Oskar Stålberg[/i]

notes.title: Hello World
notes.notes:
[i]Dear Townscapers,[/i]

It feels great to have this toy released into the wild. It is absolutely delightful to see all the wonderful towns you all are building. Townscaper blew up a bit more than I expected, and I am somewhat overwhelmed with all the feedback and support you are providing. I'm afraid that I will not able to answer all your forum posts, emails, and twitter comments, but I will adress some of the most common topics here.

But first, a summary of my personal circumstances to give you a sense of the pace of development in the near future: I'm writing this from a laptop far out on the Swedish countryside, where I'm taking at least two weeks vacation to introduce my grandparents to their first great grandchild. Back home, we just moved and are not even nearly done unpacking and setting up the new flat. Moreover, I'm gonna go on half-time parental leave in the fall, and full-time parental leave in the spring. 

I should be able to get some work done though, and here is what that work might look like:

[h3]Architeture[/h3]
Throughout updating the game, I will continously add small details and architectural patterns. These are fun to make and mostly easy to add. The way the rules for these patterns work is quite esoteric, so it is not easy to explain why some things are easy to add and others hard or impossible. Some of these I will let you know about, and some of these I will leave for you to find on your own.

[h3]MacOS[/h3]
My first priority is to release a Mac version. I'm not promising any specific date, but I will work towards this while still on vacation. I'm actually writing this on a Macbook right now (the one we bought for Bad North). The game runs perfectly fine on a Mac, but Apple has a rather elaborate security process with notarization I need to go through before I can release it to the public. And working on a Mac is new to me, so it's all a bit slow.

[h3]Linux[/h3]
I don't know much about Linux, but apparently people are running the game just fine on Linux through Proton, so I'm not gonna focus on a specific Linux release in the near future.

[h3]People?[/h3]
Many of you are suggesting I add people to the game. I would like to add more life to the game. I'm probably gonna start with some more animals; some fish or maybe a whale would be easy. Perhaps a pattern to build piers, and boats that come visit them. Adding people is a not a small task though. They need all kinds of complex behaviour, animation, and navigation, and I don't want to add them unless I feel I can make them good enough and interesting enough.

[h3]Terrain?[/h3]
Many of you are suggesting I add new types of building blocks, like terrain, beach, different architectural styles etc. This does make perfect sense from a design perspective. Unfortunately, this is actually much more technically difficult than it might seem. Townscaper is built around a complex algorithm that I feed with handcrafted puzzle pieces that handle all the different possible connections and configurations. The number of pieces I need grow exponentially with the number of features I add. Adding one new type of block would increase that number from half-a-thousand to several thousands, which is not realistic. It is not impossible that I come up with some clever way of circumventing this combinatorial explosion, but I cannot promise anything.

[h3]Bigger Grid![/h3]
People are building way bigger than I thought they would. This makes me happy. When I decided the size of the grid, I built the biggest thing I thought anyone would want to build, and then doubled that. Clearly, that was not big enough. I'm fairly certain I will make the grid bigger, but there are a few things I need to figure out before that: the game does get slow when you build too big, my lighting system bugs out, and the graphics looks a bit too repetitive. I want to investigate and resolve these issues before I increase the grid size.

[i](Also, technically, the grid is actually infinite, it is the size of your town that is limited. Before you start building, you can pan around until you find a piece of grid you like, and start building there)[/i]

[h3]My hand hurts from all the clicking![/h3]
People are building for way longer than I though they would. This makes me happy. It also makes some peoples hands hurt. Many of your are suggesting various ways, tools, and modes to be able to place multiple blocks faster to alleviate this. After much hard thinking, I have come up with a design I think will work that I will try to implement.

[h3]Bugs[/h3] 
It is a sad fact of this universe that all games have bugs on release, and Townscaper is no exception. If you are encountering bugs please tell me all about them in this [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1291340/discussions/1/]sub forum[/url], and I will do my best to fix them.

[h3]Save[/h3]
The game saves automatically when you exit the game, or when you open the save menu (the button that says "Open")

[h3]Controls[/h3]
The game does have a bunch of controls and keyboard shortcuts, but info on them (and the ability to edit them) are nowhere to be found. I will add a proper control screen in the future. In the meantime, here are the current hardcoded controls:

[b]LMB click[/b] - Add block
[b]RMB click[/b] - Remove block
[b]LMB drag[/b] - Rotate camera
[b]RMB drag[/b] - Pan camera
[b]Scroll wheel[/b] - Zoom
[b]ALT+LMB click[/b] - Select the color at the block the cursor is over
[b]WASDQE[/b] or [b]Arrow keys, Page up[/b] and [b]Page down[/b] - Move camera
[b]1234567890YUIOP[/b] - Select colors
[b]","[/b] and [b]"."[/b] - Cycle colors
[b]CTRL+Z[/b] - Undo
[b]CTRL+X[/b] - Redo



[i]Anyway, thanks a ton for enjoying Townscaper. I hope you are having as much fun playing with it as I have developing it.

Best wishes, 
Oskar Stålberg[/i]

notes.title: Lovely town-building toy Townscaper is out in early access
notes.notes:
I’ve had a lovely afternoon building quaint island towns in Townscaper, launched into early access yesterday. It’s a town-building toy where the outcome is a surprise, really. All you do is place coloured blocks, then Townscaper translates them into apartments, steps, terraces, gardens, towers, and so on based on the shapes they form with other nearby blocks, then fill the whole place with lovely little decorative details. Every town cannot help but look lovely. Its creator, Oskar Stålberg previously made several procedural landscape toys I’ve enjoyed before, and was the artist for Bad North too.

(more…)

notes.title: Procedural building toy Townscaper will let you construct lovely seaside villages
notes.notes:
This whimsical little seaside town builder is another project by Oskar Stålberg whose tiny planet and city builder projects RPS have marveled at in the past. Unlike his prior browser-based experiments, Townscaper is being treated to some extra polish and plans for a paid release. It’s been on my mental wishlist since before it had a name, but now there’s a handy page on the Steam store to help me not forget. Check out the trailer below for some extremely satisfying pips and pops as the rainbow cities spring from the sea.
